entries.subject: DAMIT 454: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-454.txt. Model 454, version 2012-07-30, pole (45°, 44°), period 3.396232 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Other DAMIT shape solutions
entries.finding: The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 455: pole (197°, 31°), 3.396233 h, version 2012-07-30. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: Independent shape, spin or scale evidence distinguishes these alternatives, or a changed release offers a demonstrably better supported model.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA thermal scale
entries.finding: The retained AcuA row 699 (Hela; four detections) supplies a 13.39 ± 0.45 km fitted nonrotating-sphere effective diameter. The recipe transfers it uniformly to the uncalibrated DAMIT 454 mesh as an approximate volume scale. The catalog error is thermal-model/statistical only; it does not establish total size uncertainty, local shape accuracy, terrain or imagery. The retrieved original catalogue row was compared field-for-field with the retained row and matches.

entries.subject: Historical model and population records
entries.finding: Historical review retained the Marciniak et al. (2012) model-publication record and JPL SBDB Mars-crosser classification from the former README survey. They provide source context only: neither selects between the two DAMIT poles nor qualifies terrain, imagery or the AKARI scale.
